notes: The PDF's own filename says the cycle begins in 09/2026, but the document's own title, header ('07/2026-12/2026 Diocesan Cycle of Prayer') and repeated page footer ('07/2026 – 12/2026 Diocesan Cycle of Prayer', dated 06-16-2026) all state the true coverage as July-December 2026, and the content itself begins with a July 5, 2026 entry -- confirmed by rendering both PDF pages as images at 150dpi and visually cross-checking them against the pdftotext -layout extraction. Actual coverage transcribed here is 2026-07-05 through 2026-12-27 (July-December 2026); January-June 2026 is simply not part of this document, not a gap in this transcription.
This source is a single-column, two-page layout (verified visually per the above) -- no multi-column interleaving risk was found, unlike some other sources flagged elsewhere in this corpus.
Nearly every date is a Sunday, but two are not, preserved exactly as printed rather than corrected: September 19, 2026 (a Saturday) and December 24, 2026 (Christmas Eve, a Thursday).
No entry in this source carries an explicit liturgical Sunday name/label (e.g. 'Proper 21') anywhere -- `liturgicalNote` is therefore null throughout.

Judgment call on subject modeling: where the source names a specific congregation together with a trailing named clergyperson (e.g. 'St. Andrew's Episcopal Church, Highland Park, and the Rev. Sara Irwin'), the congregation is recorded as a `parish` subject (name/place split at the comma separating them) and the accompanying clergy phrase is preserved verbatim in that subject's own `note` field, since this schema has no dedicated field for an individually named accompanying clergyperson. Where the source instead names a collective category with an enumerated list of individuals (e.g. 'Retired clergy, including the Rev. ... and the Rev. ...'), the entire line is kept as ONE `category` subject's `name` string rather than split into one subject per person, matching how episcopal-colorado-2026.json's own 'The Northwest Region of our Diocese and its Missioner, the Rev. Jeremy Lucas' entry keeps a region-plus-missioner phrase as a single category name.

October 25, 2026 names two parishes (Kittanning and Rural Valley) followed by a single trailing clergy name ('the Rev. Brandon Cooper') with no indication in the source of which parish he is attached to; it is recorded as a `note` on the second (Rural Valley) parish subject as the nearer antecedent in the sentence -- an interpretive choice, not stated by the source itself.

The Northern Cambria parish appears twice under two different printed forms of its own name, both preserved exactly as printed rather than harmonized: 'St. Thomas' (September 19 entry) and 'St. Thomas Episcopal Church' (October 4 entry, which otherwise repeats the same parish/clergy pairing as September 19 -- not an error in this transcription, the source's own content).

August 30, 2026's entry contains an apparent typo in the source, a period where a comma is expected ('the Very Rev. Canon John Park. the Rev. Lorena Ringle') -- preserved verbatim per this corpus's standing rule against silently correcting a source document.
Curly apostrophes (’) as used in the source's own congregation names (e.g. 'St. Luke’s', 'St. Bartholomew’s') are preserved exactly as printed rather than normalized to straight apostrophes.

Punctuation/comma placement around the trailing 'and the Rev. ...' clergy phrase varies between entries in the source itself (e.g. a comma before 'and' in most entries, but none in the November 8 and December 13 entries) -- each entry's own note field preserves the source's own wording/spacing as printed, not normalized to a single consistent style.
